title: 1983 AHSME Problem 16
statement: Let \[ \begin{aligned} x&=0.123456789101112\\ &\phantom{={}}\ldots998999, \end{aligned} \] where the digits are obtained by writing the integers \(1\) through \(999\) in order. The \(1983\)rd digit to the right of the decimal point is

solutions.text:
The one-digit integers contribute \(9\) digits and the two-digit integers contribute \(90\cdot2=180,\) for \(189\) total. Thus the desired digit is the \(1983-189=1794\)th digit among the three-digit integers. Since \(1794=598\cdot3,\) it is the last digit of the \(598\)th three-digit integer, namely \(100+597=697.\) That digit is \(7.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: First count the digits contributed by the one- and two-digit integers
After \(189\) digits, locate the remaining position within the three-digit integers
